evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'this should take about five to ten minutes of your time so we can build an accurate code' but then rushes past without waiting for explicit yes—customer has to interject about timing.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Chris Piedra), moving day (November 5th), route (Kyle, TX to Maxville, TX), size (1200 sq ft origin, 2500 sq ft destination) all confirmed.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing has already begun—rep asked name, email, how heard about company, current address, zip code, then asks 'Do you have any biggest concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' Customer says no.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised no concerns, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns raised, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (house/mobile home), stories (1 story origin, 2 story destination), bedrooms (3 at origin, 5 at destination but only moving to 3), additional rooms (shed/garage), parking (driveway), access concerns (none identified), box count (45–55 range, customer agrees), large items (standard furniture only). All seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. Rep says 'no need help I packing this is from point eight to point B' which appears to be a miscommunication/unclear phrasing but does not ask the packing services question.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes—'a typical a back count based on your home size would be 45 to 55 boxes do you feel that you fall within that range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full—rep gives typical range ('a typical 1200 square foot home would normally takes two movers and one truck that is between six to eight hours') and personalizes to this move ('we're coming from a one bedroom or sorry a one story house going to a two story house which is like less than twenty minutes away'). Estimated cost $1,854 provided.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full—trip fee ($190) disclosed upfront, all-inclusive scope explained ($104/hr, 26ft truck, gas, taxes, insurance, tools, bonds all included). Minimum 2.5 hours mentioned, 15-minute increments explained, no hidden fees stated explicitly.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep gives estimate and explanation but never asks 'does that feel fair?' or similar. Customer naturally asks clarifying questions about truck size and deposit requirements instead.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full—'we have on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full—'we have no worry damage coverage. Included on the early rate that you're paying us. They will provide up to 2000 dollars per move that is to repair, replace and reimburse for your items.' Explicitly stated as included, no deductible/fine print mentioned but framed as built-in.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No—rep does not ask 'does that put those to rest?' or similar confirmation. After listing the perks and explaining pricing mechanics, rep pivots directly to the ask.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway—rep never asks 'what's still concerning you about this move?' After customer says no to the explicit ask (would rather shop around), rep offers to send email and says 'feel free to call us email or text us' but no genuine final concerns check occurs.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No—never asks 'anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full—'Would you like our help with your move and lock that in for you today?' asked plainly with no built-in out.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False—never mentioned that the quote is rate-locked or valid for a specific period.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None—customer declines ('Not yet, I'm still kinda calling around'). No booking details confirmed (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, crew notes) because the customer did not commit. Rep offers to send email quote but does not attempt to lock anything in.

top_strength: Excellent discovery and logistics gathering—rep systematically covered all seven logistics items and confirmed both properties thoroughly, including stories, bedrooms, access, parking, and special items, enabling an accurate estimate.
coaching_note: You must ask 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate and hold the silence—this is your last chance to hear objections before the ask, and rushing past it leaves money on the table; also, skip the early-call concerns question after you've already started probing, or wait until you've gathered details, but don't sandwích it between name-capture and logistics.
